figures.headline: Full attention shows the highest video loss with large spikes, and removing video guidance degrades it most.
citing_sentences: Fig .20 and Fig. 21 show the video and audio training loss during native high-resolution training.

In Fig. 20(a) and Fig. 21(a), Full Attn exhibits the highest video loss with extreme instability and persistent large spikes throughout training, revealing that the massive redundant tokens at 2K not only dilute attention weights on informative interactions but also inject severe noise into the optimization trajectory, preventing stable convergence.

In Fig. 20(b) and Fig. 21(b), the asymmetric degradation pattern reveals the complementary roles of the two guidance signals. w/o Video Guidance causes the most severe video loss degradation with frequent large spikes, while its audio loss degrades moderately, confirming that video channel-wise variance is the primary driver for concentrating gradients on visually informative regions. w/o Audio Guidance yields a lower video loss than w/o Video Guidance yet produces a noticeably higher and rising audio loss, revealing that audio-to-video cross-attention norm guidance primarily governs cross-modal stability rather than visual quality.

abstract: Natively training joint video-audio generation models at higher resolutions empowers them to learn richer visual details and sharper motion dynamics. However, full attention incurs quadratic cost and, as resolution increases, spreads attention over increasingly redundant tokens, diluting learning signals for informative content and disrupting pretrained priors. Existing sparse attention methods either target training-free acceleration or overlook the unique structure of joint video-audio data, where cross-modal interactions are inherently concentrated around sound-producing regions. To address this, we propose Prism, a dynamic sparse attention framework for natively training joint video-audio generation models at 2K. In particular, Prism organizes the token sequence into spatiotemporal macro-zones, enabling the attention structure to adapt to local content. For each zone, it estimates local information structure via video feature variance along the channel and feature norms from the audio-to-video cross-attention, jointly capturing how visual content varies directionally and how strongly audio influences each visual region. Based on these signals, Prism dynamically assigns a tailored block shape to each zone, applying finer partitioning along axes of rapid visual content variation and strong audio-visual coupling. This encourages tokens within each block to remain semantically coherent, allowing block-level features to capture both visual content and joint video-audio interaction patterns. Prism further adopts a hybrid block selection strategy to dynamically determine per-query sparsity. Experiments show that Prism achieves 2.5$\times$ training speedup compared to full attention, while surpassing it in generation quality.

sections.body: The introduction states that a 2K clip of 12s at FPS=24 yields over one million tokens under VAE compression, and that repetitive background tokens take up most of the attention weight. Prior sparse methods are mostly training-free or trained only at 480P or 720P, and they ignore audio-visual coupling. The authors propose Prism, which assigns each spatiotemporal macro-zone a 3D block shape and selects key blocks with a hybrid top-k and top-p rule. They report 2.5 times training speedup over full attention while achieving better quality.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Full attention at 2K is quadratically costly and dilutes attention on informative tokens, so fixed sparse patterns fall short.

sections.body: This section groups related work into three areas. Joint video-audio generation models such as MOVA, LTX-2.3 and Ovi scale parameters and data but cannot train natively at 2K. Efficient attention covers linear attention, training-free sparse attention, and a few trainable sparse methods such as VMoBA and SpargeAttention2, which use fixed block shapes or layer-indexed partitions. Native high-resolution work, including UltraGen, T3 and the cascaded PyramidFlow, relies on fixed-shape windows or coarse-to-fine pipelines. The authors state that none of these account for cross-modal coupling in joint video-audio data.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior joint video-audio models do not train natively at 2K, and trainable sparse methods use fixed block shapes.

sections.body: Prism applies block-sparse attention only to video self-attention, since it dominates cost at 2K. The video token grid is split into macro-zones of 8 along each axis, and each zone is tiled by 3D blocks with edge lengths of 2, 4 or 8, because the Triton kernel uses a 64-token tile. For each zone, per attention head and layer, the method combines the variance of value features across each axis with the normalized audio-to-video cross-attention norm. Attention then runs over the top-k blocks together with the top-p blocks, so the number of attended blocks varies per query. Training uses the video and audio flow matching losses.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: Prism assigns each macro-zone a 3D block shape from video variance and audio coupling, then selects key blocks per query.

sections.body: Prism is initialized from MOVA and trained on 100k 2K clips for 5 epochs at a learning rate of 1e-5, with top-k 95% and top-p 0.2. On 2K-Bench, a set of 300 unseen 2K videos of 10 seconds, Table 1 shows Prism ahead of Ovi, LTX-2.3, MagiHuman and MOVA on every listed metric. On 720p VABench and MOVA-Bench the margin is smaller, which the authors attribute to shorter sequences with less redundancy. In ablations, Prism improves over SpargeAttention2 by 46% in MotionQ and 30% in DeSync. The section also notes that commercial models still lead in visual realism and audio aesthetics.
sections.heading: Experiment
sections.headline: On 2K-Bench, Prism beats four open-source baselines on every metric in Table 1.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the method. Prism organizes tokens into spatiotemporal macro-zones and assigns each zone a 3D block shape from video channel-wise variance and audio-to-video cross-attention norms. A hybrid strategy sets per-query sparsity. The section repeats the reported result: 2.5 times training speedup compared with full attention at 2K, while surpassing it in generation quality. It introduces no new experiments and does not restate the limitations.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Prism pairs macro-zone block shapes with hybrid selection and reports 2.5 times training speedup over full attention at 2K.

sections.body: The appendix contains Tables 3 to 7, a preliminaries section on rectified flow, and definitions of the video, audio, synchronization and motion metrics. Table 14 reports a user study with 200 participants, using two-alternative forced choice on 30 videos, in which Prism is preferred over Ovi, LTX-2.3, MagiHuman and MOVA. It also covers consent for human-subject data, misuse safeguards, and a failure case. The stated limitation is that rapid camera focus changes cause blurriness or body distortion, because macro-zones span a fixed 8 frames. Scaling beyond 2K and larger backbones are left for future work.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists extra tables, metric definitions, the user study, ethics and limitations, and further visualizations.
